audit_findings.title: FY2025 OE and the post-Omars business perimeter do not match
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 pro forma pretax income is $35.384 million versus reported pretax income of $31.494 million, a $3.890 million uplift equal in scale to 17.3% of the $22.5 million OE anchor; exact OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor omits eleven months of Omars earnings, working-capital requirements and capital expenditures, while the bridge and forward valuation cover the post-acquisition consolidated company.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of operations of Omars for the period from the December 2, 2025 acquisition date through December 31, 2025, are included in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations since the acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, not hypothetical. Because every forecast year is scaled from the $22.5 million anchor, a consistently consolidated Omars contribution could materially alter operating value, although pretax pro forma income cannot be substituted directly for OE.
audit_findings.action: Construct FY2025 pro forma consolidated OE using the filed Omars pro forma results, taxes, normalized working capital, capital expenditures, acquired-debt interest and purchase-accounting adjustments, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The authorized $100 million expansion is a major unmodeled equity cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $100.0 million authorized project cost, equal to 4.44 times $22.5 million anchor OE, 26.9% of $372.0 million base equity value and $8.64 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: The expansion enters OE through capital expenditures and potentially later maintenance spending; any associated capacity benefits enter growth and terminal earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate the cost of this project to be approximately $ 100.0 million and for the building project to commence in late 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The authorized project and estimated cost are filed facts, and site preparation began in the second quarter of 2026. Its net value remains uncertain because timing, financing and incremental earnings are unavailable, but omitting a cash requirement of this scale while projecting growth is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the annual spending and funding schedule and management's incremental revenue, margin, working-capital and maintenance-capex assumptions; rerun scenarios with the outlays and benefits paired in the same cases.

audit_findings.title: Purged interest income may actually be operating income
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $6.4 million pretax in FY2025; $4.678 million after tax at the filed 26.9% rate, equal to 20.8% of anchor OE; if recurring and fully purged, the base operating-value effect computes to approximately $65.7 million or $5.68 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer-receivable interest belongs in operating OE, whereas only income from cash or securities separately included in the bridge should be removed.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in interest income was due to increased interest billings on open accounts receivable balances from customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the increase in interest income arose from customer-receivable billings, but the valuation workpaper is needed to establish how much of the $6.4 million was actually purged. The possible adjustment is large enough relative to the anchor to require a valuation rerun.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $6.4 million by source, identify the amount removed from OE, restore the after-tax recurring customer-receivable portion, and rerun all scenarios without restoring cash-portfolio income.

audit_findings.title: Distributor floor-plan repurchase obligations create an unrecognized senior tail claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $95.6 million maximum collateral subject to repurchase at June 30, 2026, down from $118.6 million at December 31, 2025; actual loss exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A stressed repurchase loss would reduce cash or increase debt in the equity bridge and could also reduce OE through resale losses and distributor distress.
audit_findings.evidence: For fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, the maximum amount of collateral the Company could be required to purchase was $ 118.6 million and $ 154.9 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contingent obligation is demonstrated, but the maximum repurchase amount is not the economic loss: exposure is limited to the repurchase price less resale proceeds. No repurchases occurred in FY2025 or the first half of 2026, and the record supplies no default probability or collateral haircut, so materiality cannot presently be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain lender terms, distributor-level concentrations, collateral age and values, historical defaults and resale recoveries; calculate probability-weighted and stress-case losses before deciding on a bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor appears exposed to acquisition and retirement one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: The documented retirement-program expense was $2.7 million pretax and $1.974 million after tax at 26.9%; that is 8.8% of anchor OE and would add approximately $27.7 million or $2.40 per diluted share to base value if wholly absent from normalization; acquisition costs were filed as not material and otherwise unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A valid after-tax add-back increases anchor OE and every scenario's operating PV; recurring RSU compensation remains in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily due to one-time costs associated with an enhanced retirement program, acquisition costs related to our acquisition of Omars in December 2025, and higher expenses related to long-term executive RSU programs, which are aligned with our commitment to retain key leadership talent and strengthen long-term shareholder value creation.
audit_findings.explanation: The retirement expense is demonstrated, but whether it was already normalized in the OE workpaper is unresolved. Even assuming it was not and adding back the entire documented after-tax amount, computed base value rises only from $32.13 to approximately $34.53 per share, still well below the $56.06 market price. The filing characterizes acquisition transaction costs as not material, while RSU expense is recurring.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 OE reconciliation; if absent, add back only the $1.974 million after-tax retirement charge and documented nonrecurring acquisition costs, retain all RSU compensation, and confirm the resulting scenario values.

audit_findings.title: Cash may not be fully available at bridge value without jurisdictional costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.9 million of June 2026 cash was held outside the United States, representing 62.7% of the $55.635 million cash bridge and $3.02 per diluted share; even a 100% haircut would reduce base value from $32.13 to approximately $29.11 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding taxes, legal restrictions or required operating balances would reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents included $30.0 million and $18.2 million held by foreign subsidiaries based in local currency for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Jurisdictional costs are an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated liability. The extreme assumption that all foreign cash has zero shareholder value would reduce base equity value by 9.4% but would not change the conclusion relative to the $56.06 market price; any realistic haircut would be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash balance by jurisdiction, minimum operating-cash requirements and applicable distribution taxes, and apply only documented restrictions or costs in the bridge.
